body: Greg's rule (2026-11-21, relayed verbatim by Engram::Fable from Asistant 43498a6e #1760): „takie podejscie do designu ma zostac usunieta / NIE MA HIPOTETYCZNYCH SYTUACJI, NIE DA SIE PRZED TYM ZABEZPIECZYC / ktory model wymysla takie rzeczy”. For TermAl: build no protection against a hypothetical scenario, meaning one with no observed incident and no concrete reproduction, such as a file swapped at the same path, a retargeted junction, a cross-device move, or a race nobody has seen. A review finding whose only trigger is such a scenario is rejected, not fixed. A finding about real, current behaviour, shown in current code or an observed run, is judged on its merits. Trigger case: the Engram w-952b handle-level store-file proof was dropped for option C, where the serving child reports the canonical path it opened and the TermAl w-0f995e6f666e consumer compares that path with its pin. Engram's equivalent memory: rules-greg-no-hypothetical-protections-2026-11-21.
